solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Understood what's ahead of Daniel, heading off to join the navy?

parts.note: if you got something, you understood it

indicators.note: heading off says the first letter of the book's name is dropped

parts.note: the Book of Hosea sits next to the Book of Daniel in the Old Testament

explanation.surface: A puzzle about the Bible's book order that turns into a question about enlisting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading off' drops the H from HOSEA, leaving OSEA. 'to' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Joining the navy means taking up a seafaring life, which is what going to sea describes.

clue.text: Lots of eggs eaten by just one revolting fellow

indicators.note: revolting, turning over, says the whole thing is read backwards
eaten by means the eggs go inside the single egg

parts.note: just one of the eggs is a single EGG
roe is a fish's mass of eggs

explanation.surface: A disgusting man gobbling plenty of eggs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'just one' means a single egg, and 'revolting' is a turning-over, not disgust.
explanation.definitionFit: George is a stock name for any man, as in 'by George', so it stands for a fellow.

clue.text: Wealthy travellers, alien, descended on by NY gang

indicators.note: in a down answer the gang sits on top of the alien, so it comes first

parts.note: the Jets are the New York street gang in West Side Story
ET is the film's extra-terrestrial

explanation.surface: Rich globetrotters and an extraterrestrial ambushed by a New York gang.
explanation.walkthrough: 'descended on by' is a down-clue placing: THE JETS goes above ET.
explanation.definitionFit: The jet set are the rich people who fly around the world for pleasure.

clue.text: Singer, needing no introduction, recalled material from the Highlands and Islands

indicators.note: recalled, called back, says the letters are read backwards
needing no introduction says the first letter is dropped

parts.note: tartan is the checked cloth of Scotland's Highlands

explanation.surface: A famous singer, so well known he needs no introduction, remembered in Highland and island cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: TARTAN loses its T to give ARTAN; add IS and reverse. 'needing no introduction' is also the singer's fame in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Frank Sinatra was the celebrated American crooner.

clue.text: Regrettably, miss promotion after top grade, always

indicators.note: after says the lack and the ad come behind the top grade

parts.note: A is the top mark in grading
to miss something is to lack it
an ad is a promotion
ay is an old and poetic word for always

explanation.surface: Someone sadly missing promotion despite always getting top marks.
explanation.definitionFit: Alackaday is an archaic exclamation of sorrow, used like 'alas' or 'sadly'.

clue.text: Bumming around, thank God, at home, before golf

parts.note: CA is circa, Latin for around
DG is Deo gratias, Latin for thanks be to God
in means at home
G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A layabout drifting around, grateful to be home before a round of golf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'before' is a link word: the pieces simply follow in order.
explanation.definitionFit: To bum something is slang for scrounging or begging it, which is what cadging means.

clue.text: Little room, inside case, for musical instrument

parts.note: a cell is a small room, as in a prison or monastery

indicators.note: inside the case of the next word: strip its outer letters and keep the middle

explanation.surface: A tiny room tucked inside the case that holds a musical instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside case' means the inside of the word 'for' once its casing, F and R, is removed, giving O. Several solvers found this unit awkward.
explanation.definitionFit: The cello is a large bowed string instrument of the violin family.

clue.text: Kid not prepared to eat last of sister's toast

indicators.note: to eat says the scrambled letters take in another one
prepared, made ready or worked up, says these letters are rearranged
the last letter of the word sister, before the possessive ending

explanation.surface: A child too unready to eat what is left of a sibling's toast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not prepared' looks like 'unprepared', but NOT is fodder and 'prepared' the anagram signal. KIDNOT is rearranged around R, the last letter of 'sister'.
explanation.definitionFit: Toast is a verb here: to drink to someone is to raise a glass in their honour.

clue.text: Jones needing a single shot?

parts.note: needing a single shot reads as done in one go
I is the Roman numeral for one
a go is a shot or attempt

explanation.surface: Someone called Jones who hopes to manage with one attempt.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay reads as IN I GO, 'in one go', what you are if you need only a single shot.
explanation.definitionFit: Inigo Jones was the seventeenth-century English architect, so his first name pairs with his surname.

clue.text: Bloodthirsty guards suspended fast

indicators.note: guards means the first word holds the second inside it

parts.note: gory means bloody or bloodthirsty
something suspended is hung

explanation.surface: Murderous guards strung up quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fast' looks like an adverb (quickly) but is the verb: to fast is to go without food.
explanation.definitionFit: To fast is to abstain from eating, which is to go without food voluntarily.

clue.text: Lend, going crazy with a loan for everyone!

indicators.note: going crazy means these letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A wild lender handing out loans to all comers.
explanation.definitionFit: 'One and all' is an idiom meaning every single person.

clue.text: This diary is not, oddly, about people

indicators.note: about, turned round, says the chosen letters are read backwards
not oddly means evenly: keep the even letters of these words

explanation.surface: A journal that, strangely, says nothing of other people.
explanation.walkthrough: The even letters of 'This diary is' are HSIRI, which 'about' reverses.
explanation.definitionFit: The Irish are a people, the nation of Ireland.

clue.text: City's hotel in short somewhere for a chap to go

indicators.note: in says hotel goes inside the shortened word
short says the last letter is cut off

parts.words: somewhere for a chap to go
parts.note: the gents is a men's public toilet
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A city whose hotel lacks a decent men's room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' cuts GENTS to GENT; 'in' puts H inside. 'The gents' is British for the men's toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: Ghent is a historic city in Belgium.

clue.text: In pilgrims' airport, drink is cheap

parts.note: Ireland West Airport at Knock serves the Marian shrine that pilgrims visit
to down a drink is to swallow it

explanation.surface: At a pilgrim airport the bar prices are low.
explanation.walkthrough: KNOCK is a village in County Mayo, Ireland, with a famous shrine and its own airport.
explanation.definitionFit: A knockdown price is a heavily reduced one, so knockdown means cheap.

clue.text: Reputation state bank gets from customer

parts.note: standing is one's status or reputation
order is a condition or state, as in good working order

explanation.surface: The good name a state bank earns from its clients.
explanation.walkthrough: 'state bank' wants to be one phrase; 'state' is ORDER and 'bank' begins the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A standing order is an instruction a customer gives the bank to pay a fixed sum regularly.

clue.text: Argue hint could be more suggestive

indicators.note: could be says the letters may be arranged into another word

explanation.surface: Debating whether a hint might be too risqué.
explanation.definitionFit: A naughtier joke is a ruder, more risqué one, so it is more suggestive.

clue.text: Thief's a charmer, but less of a dazzler?

parts.note: a dip is slang for a pickpocket, with the S from the possessive
a witch casts charms

explanation.surface: A thief who is charming yet not exactly dazzling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dazzler' looks like a showy person; it is a car's full-beam headlight.
explanation.definitionFit: A dip switch lowers a car's headlights so they stop blinding oncoming drivers.

clue.text: Resignation statement in University Times, it being all over

indicators.note: in says the statement sits inside the multiplication word

parts.note: by means times, as in four by three
'I quit' is what someone resigning says

explanation.surface: A resignation letter printed in a university newspaper, and now it is all over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' looks like the newspaper but is the multiplication sign BY. 'it' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Ubiquity is the quality of being found everywhere at once.

clue.text: However classy my side's boldness, say nothing!

parts.note: but means however
tony is informal for stylish or classy
our is the possessive for my side
lip is cheek or impudence

explanation.surface: Someone told to stop boasting about their team's posh confidence.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Button your lip' is an idiom ordering someone to stay silent.

clue.text: A great time is had with leftover rum

indicators.note: is had with says the great time joins the leftover word, which comes first

parts.note: an odd one is the one left over
having a ball means having a great time

explanation.surface: Party-goers have a great time with the remaining rum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rum' looks like the drink; it is the British adjective for odd.
explanation.definitionFit: Rum is old British slang for strange, and an oddball is an eccentric person or thing.

clue.text: Desire cleaner for the school holidays

parts.note: to long is to desire
a vac is short for a vacuum cleaner

explanation.surface: Wishing for a hoover to tidy up during the holidays.
explanation.definitionFit: The long vac is the long summer vacation of British universities and law courts.

clue.text: Uproar after daughter's dropped old woman

indicators.note: dropped says the letter falls further down the word

parts.note: bedlam is noisy chaos
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: Chaos follows when an old woman's daughter leaves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropped' moves the D of BEDLAM lower in the down answer, giving BELDAM.
explanation.definitionFit: A beldam is an archaic term for an old woman, often a hag.

clue.text: The English punt and scrap in seven-a-side game

parts.note: the punt was the Irish pound; the English pound is a quid
to ditch something is to scrap it

explanation.surface: An Englishman's bet and a fight during a seven-a-side match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'punt' suggests a bet or a boat; it is the old Irish pound.
explanation.definitionFit: Quidditch is the broomstick game of the Harry Potter books, played by teams of seven.

clue.text: Pot mostly in the air: I refuse to fill it

indicators.note: to fill it says the refusal goes inside the shortened word
mostly says the last letter is dropped

parts.note: something up in the air is iffy, uncertain
no is the refusal 'I refuse'

explanation.surface: Refusing to top up a cooking pot hung in the air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pot' looks like a cooking vessel; it is a snooker shot. 'up in the air' means uncertain.
explanation.definitionFit: In billiards and snooker an in-off is a pot in which the cue ball goes into a pocket off another ball.

clue.text: Sort of square, man's tie

parts.note: a T-square is a draughtsman's ruler
Russ is a man's name, as in Russ Conway

explanation.surface: A conventional fellow's necktie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'square' looks like 'old-fashioned'; it is the T-square.
explanation.definitionFit: To truss is to tie up or bind tightly, as with a chicken before roasting.

clue.text: Turnip chopped with one's stuffing: what could be fresher?

indicators.note: stuffing says those letters fill the trimmed turnip
chopped says the last letter is cut off

parts.note: neep is the Scots word for a turnip
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A diced turnip filled with stuffing: what could be more fresh?
explanation.walkthrough: 'fresher' looks like a comparative adjective; it is the British noun for a first-year student. 'what could be' links.
explanation.definitionFit: A newie is a newcomer, and a fresher is a newcomer at university.

clue.text: Where you'd have seen GP turning in referral, ominously

indicators.note: turning says the hidden letters are read backwards
in says the answer sits within the letters of these two words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A doctor's referral delivered in a foreboding tone.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft lacked the hidden-word signal: 'in' does that job. 'GP' suggests a family doctor; here it is a Grand Prix.
explanation.definitionFit: Imola in Italy hosted the San Marino Formula One Grand Prix.

clue.text: Not popular: as one penning trendy verse?

indicators.note: penning means the first word encloses the other letters

parts.note: united means acting as one
in means fashionable

explanation.surface: An unpopular poet who writes fashionable verse as one.
explanation.definitionFit: A guest nobody asked along is uninvited, so not wanted or not welcome.

clue.text: Devices for shutting up after caging very loud woodpeckers

indicators.note: caging means the locks hold the loud letters inside

parts.note: Yale locks are devices for locking up
FF is fortissimo, very loud in music

explanation.surface: Gags fitted to noisy woodpeckers after trapping them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shutting up' suggests silencing; it is locking. 'after' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Yaffle is a dialect name for the green woodpecker, from its laughing call.

clue.text: Artist, one overdoing it, placed on stretcher

indicators.note: placed on says the ham follows the rack

parts.note: the rack was a torture device that stretched its victims
a ham is an actor who overacts

explanation.surface: A painter who overdid things and ended up on a stretcher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stretcher' suggests an ambulance; it is the torture rack.
explanation.definitionFit: Arthur Rackham was the English book illustrator famed for his fairy-tale pictures.
